transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I’m here because I just keep blowing up at people over nothing. I've been snapping at my team on operations calls, and then I come home and do the exact same thing to my family. That is just not how I’ve ever handled things before, so... I figured I needed to come in and figure out what's going on.
Outside of those moments when you snap, how has your overall mood been lately?

Honestly, it's just been really flat. Empty, I guess. Like, my wife will make dinner, or my kids will be talking about soccer like normal, and... I know I should feel glad to be there with them. But it’s like there’s just nothing in me that can respond. I don't feel much of anything good right now.
About how long have you been feeling this flat, empty way?
It's been about three weeks now. It all started right after... well, we had a major valve failure at the facility, and someone got hurt. Ever since then, I've just been feeling this way.
Since that accident happened, have you been having unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about it?

Yeah, I have. I can just be sitting at the kitchen table, or... trying to answer some work emails from home, and suddenly I’m right back there. I see the flash from that valve, and the smoke in the aisle... it's like it just shoves everything else right out of my head.
Have you found yourself actively trying to avoid thoughts, feelings, or reminders of the accident?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't been trying to hide from it or stay away from things. I'm still checking my work emails and talking to the guys from the plant. So I wouldn't say I'm actively avoiding thinking about it... it just kind of forces its way into my head whether I want it to or not.
Have you noticed feeling constantly on edge, watchful, or unusually jumpy since the accident?

Yeah, definitely. It's... honestly, any time I hear a forklift beep, or a compressor kick on, my whole body just tightens up. Even at home, if the smoke alarm just chirps, I instantly tense up and start looking for exits. It's like I'm just constantly scanning the room, waiting to see what's going to go wrong next.

opening_question.question: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient experienced a traumatic industrial accident three weeks ago resulting in injury to a colleague. Since the incident, the patient has developed recurrent intrusive memories and flashbacks, emotional numbing and inability to experience positive emotions, persistent hypervigilance, exaggerated startle response, and irritability with outbursts, fulfilling the diagnostic criteria for Post-traumatic stress disorder (F43.1).

confirmed_symptoms: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories and flashbacks of the industrial accident
Emotional numbing, flat affect, and persistent inability to experience positive emotions
Irritable behavior and angry outbursts with little or no provocation
Hypervigilance and scanning environments for danger
Heightened startle response to sudden noises
